description: ALIGNED clause (the subject of the entry is aligned on the first bit of the first available byte boundary, with implicit filler bits per 8.5.1.6.3), ISO §2023:13.18.1 - a COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 data description entry (§1985:VI.5.3.2, whose printed format runs `IS character-string BINARY COMPUTATIONAL COMP` ...) offers after the level-number and data-name-1 or FILLER only the REDEFINES, PICTURE, USAGE (BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL, DISPLAY, INDEX, PACKED-DECIMAL), SIGN, OCCURS, SYNCHRONIZED, JUSTIFIED, BLANK WHEN ZERO and VALUE clauses (the Inter-Program Communication module's level-01 entry adds IS EXTERNAL and IS GLOBAL, §1985:X.4.3.1: "a level 01 data description entry within the Working-Storage Section or File Section determines whether the data record and its subordinate data items have local names"), and 1985 has no bit data at all; §2002:13.16.1 adds "The ALIGNED clause specifies that a bit group item or an elementary bit data item is to be aligned at the first bit of the first available byte" (§2002:13.16.1.3 GR1: "An ALIGNED clause causes the subject of the entry to be aligned on the first bit of the first available byte boundary"), §2002:F.1 item 6 ("The following reserved words have been added") lists ALIGNED, and §2002:F.2 item 8 states the bit facility it serves: "The capability of defining bit strings and setting or testing boolean values is added." §2014:13.18.1 and §2023:13.18.1.1 carry the 2002 sentence unchanged. kb/Work PB487.

   05 B1 PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT.
   05 B2 PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT ALIGNED.
